was downgraded by Citi on Thursday as the investment firm said the storage company's opportunity in artificial intelligence is real, albeit "premature."

"Dropbox is pursuing a new strategy to drive growth based on 3 pillars: 1) stabilize the core, 2) create new content workflow products, and 3) leverage its exabyte-scale storage infra alongside existing file system, content-processing, context and governance capabilities to address fast-growing AI workloads (20%+ CAGR market)," Citi analyst Steven Enders wrote in a note to clients. "Potential differentiation could come from a bundled offering coupled with neutrality vs. hyperscalers/frontier labs. Still, Pillar 3 remains at an early eval stage, with no disclosed product, pricing, production customers, or revenue. We see key hurdles: productizing infrastructure built primarily for internal use, establishing competitive unit economics, and developing a new GTM motion. The Backblaze/CoreWeave deal supports the broader thesis that AI infrastructure demand can extend into third-party capacity storage, yet we view this as not representative of the type of deals or scale that DBX is likely to pursue."
Enders lowered his rating on Dropbox to Sell from Neutral and cut his price target to $29 from $33.

title: Dropbox downgraded at Citi as firm says AI opportunity is 'premature'
